Renal caliceal abnormalities and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; both occur in 80-99%.
Purely psychiatric personality disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the neurologic phenotype; skeletal abnormalities and joint dislocations also define the syndrome.
Brucella infection; hepatic dysfunction, arthritis and anemia/leukopenia each annotated at 30-79%. GI symptoms lack demonstrated damage; neurologic disease is uncommon.
Defined by trigeminal nerve damage with sensory loss and persistent facial skin ulceration.
Malignant mesothelioma arising in the pleura.
Following the supplied Down syndrome ancestry: neurodevelopmental impairment is defining; congenital heart defects occur in ~40-50%. Balanced wording is atypical.
XP/Cockayne overlap defines photosensitive skin disease and neurodegeneration; ocular degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss are common (>30%) in the overlap phenotype.
Retinol transport disorder causes retinal dystrophy; comedonal acne and follicular hyperkeratosis occurred in 2/2 patients.
Toxic peripheral nerve injury after organophosphate exposure; weakness reflects neuropathy rather than primary muscle disease.
Inherited generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures.
Retinal and choroidal atrophy with characteristic paravenous pigmentation.
Inherited elevated alpha-tryptase with mast-cell mediator manifestations; common lasting damage to additional organs is not established.
Defined by colonic adenomatous polyposis. Associated extraintestinal tumors are separately diagnosed neoplasms, not qualifying organ involvement.
Congenital structural defect of a tricuspid valve leaflet.
Monogenic systemic autoimmunity; lupus nephritis is a major direct manifestation in 11/17 patients (~65%).
Persistent central visual-processing dysfunction; ocular examinations are usually normal. Tinnitus and other associated symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Developmental delay, brachycephaly and hair abnormalities define BTDD; structural oral abnormalities, including cleft palate and supernumerary tooth, occur in 1/2 patients.
Inherited atrial arrhythmia with frequent cardiac chamber enlargement; all manifestations remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Arteriovenous malformation occupying the mandible defines vascular and jaw involvement; gingival bleeding alone does not establish additional GI damage.
Purine salvage disorder; neurologic dysfunction affects most patients across the severe and intermediate forms (>30%). Gout and urinary stones are separate diseases.
Benign neoplasm of bile duct epithelium; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts both belong to the hepatic axis.
Across the main subtypes, skeletal dysplasia and sparse hair are defining; intellectual disability is concentrated in type II.
Benign hair follicle-derived tumor of the dermis or subcutis; associated syndromes do not constitute involvement by this tumor.
